input: battery_voltage_delta (charging voltage target battery_voltage_prev minus measured battery voltage, signed, 1/16 V per count; flag 1 = signed input)
output: alternator_field_duty_target (0-25600 = 0-100 % field duty) in the final else branch of cm848_filterProtectionOutput = regulator state 2 (states 0, 1 and 3 have their own branches). cm848_calculateProtectionOutputDemand overwrites the duty with the PI loop result in states 2 and 3 when operating_mode_flags bit 0x20 is set; the EEPROM dump has 0x7ca6 at EEPROM 0x16c (= RAM 0x3fd5ee through the 0x3fd482 image base in firmware/CLAUDE.md), so in this dump the bit is set and this table only presets the PI integrator on the state 1 to 2 transition. With the bit clear (table-driven mode) it is the final open-loop output
units_check: 12 breakpoints -7..+7 counts = -0.44..+0.44 V of voltage error (battery_voltage is 1/16 V per count); values 0..25600 rise with the error (battery below target -> more duty; 17408 = 68 % at zero error, 100 % at +7); 25600 = 100 % matches the 0x6400 clamp at the end of the function
evidence: cm848_dispatchProtectionOutputMode is the 4-state charging voltage regulator machine (state handlers at 0x38338 / 0x38384 / 0x383f0 / 0x3844c, disassembled); battery_voltage_delta = battery_voltage_prev - sensor_readings.battery_voltage in cm848_processProtectionVoltageOffset; alternator_field_duty_target is documented in global_variables.csv as the field duty sent by cm848_applyAlternatorFieldDuty to the C1-7 K20 generator field pin.
naming_concern: Inside this regulator cruise_state_machine_index / cruise_prev_state_index (regulator state), cruise_voltage_debounce_timer, cruise_voltage_fault_state, cold_start_fuel_ema* and can_subsystem_init_state_* (interpolator caches) are misnomers; task 029 already re-domains the state pair.

input: battery_voltage_scan_index (pass counter: incremented once per regulator pass while the machine is in state 1, zeroed in states 0 and 2), unsigned
output: alternator_field_duty_target in state 1 (soft-start ramp). State 1 follows state 0 when engine rpm is above the start threshold with no regulator fault, and ends when the duty reaches 25600 or battery_voltage_delta is no longer above its threshold, then state 2 takes over. The PI loop skips state 1, so this table drives the field in every calibration
units_check: 5 breakpoints 25, 43, 62, 81, 100 passes; cm848_phase_group_b_processing (which calls the regulator chain) runs on every second 5 ms scheduler phase, so a pass is about 10 ms and the ramp spans 0.25 s to 1.0 s; values 0, 6400, 12800, 19200, 25600 = 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 % duty in even steps
evidence: Branch cruise_state_machine_index == 1 of cm848_filterProtectionOutput sets the duty from this table, then increments battery_voltage_scan_index and zeroes battery_voltage_confirm_counter; state 0 and the state 2 branch reset the counter to 0, so it is the age of the ramp.
naming_concern: battery_voltage_scan_index is a ramp-age pass counter, not a voltage scan index.

input: battery_voltage_delta (signed, 1/16 V per count; flag 1 = signed input)
output: alternator_field_duty_target in regulator state 3 while cruise_voltage_debounce_timer is nonzero. State 3 is entered from state 2 when battery_voltage_delta_filtered (the error minus its own low-pass) exceeds a threshold, i.e. the voltage error jumps up because an electrical load was applied; the table drives the field hard for a short hold (L080), then the duty falls back to the pre-dip average and ramps (L081 x L082). Table-driven mode only: cm848_calculateProtectionOutputDemand also runs in state 3 and, with operating_mode_flags bit 0x20 set (this dump), overwrites the duty in the same pass, so none of the state 3 tables reach the field in that mode
units_check: 12 breakpoints -7..+22 counts = -0.44..+1.4 V; values 0 at -7, 25600 (100 %) from +7 upward, so the field goes full on for a dip of 0.44 V or more (the state 2 table L077 also reaches 100 % at +7 but is higher below it: 68 % at zero error vs 50 % here)
evidence: State 3 handler (0x3844c) is reached only from state 2 on battery_voltage_delta_filtered > cal threshold; on state 3 entry cold_start_fuel_ema (slow average of the duty) is snapshotted and the hold timer loaded; when the timer reaches 0 the duty is set back to the snapshot and then incremented by (L082 x L081) / 10 per pass. The load response wording is my reading of that sequence (a classic alternator load response ramp); the input, output and breakpoints are traced.
naming_concern: cruise_voltage_fault_state (values 0/1/2) is the load response stage (hold / dropped back / ramping), not a cruise fault state.

output: cruise_voltage_debounce_timer, loaded once on state 3 entry (cruise_prev_state_index != 3) and decremented once per pass; while it is nonzero the duty follows the L079 table, at zero the duty drops back to the pre-dip average (cold_start_fuel_ema_snapshot) and then ramps with L081 x L082. Table-driven mode only: the timer still runs when bit 0x20 of operating_mode_flags is set, but the PI loop overwrites the duty it gates in the same pass
units_check: 5 breakpoints 4000, 5200, 5600, 6400, 7200 counts = 500, 650, 700, 800, 900 rpm (idle region); values 3, 11, 11, 11, 11 passes of about 10 ms = 30..110 ms; the hold is shorter below 650 rpm
evidence: Only the timer semantics (hold time of the first state 3 stage) rest on the code reading above; input and output are both named and the rpm breakpoints sit in the idle band where load response matters. Unit of a pass inferred from the scheduler (phase group B every second 5 ms phase).
naming_concern: cruise_voltage_debounce_timer is a load response hold counter, not a debounce of a cruise voltage.

output: local wVar2 in cm848_filterProtectionOutput: one of two factors of the per-pass duty increment in state 3 after the hold: alternator_field_duty_target += (L082 rpm factor x this duty factor) / 10. Table-driven mode only: with operating_mode_flags bit 0x20 set (this dump) the PI loop overwrites the duty in the same pass
units_check: 5 breakpoints 0, 10240, 16384, 25600, 25600 = 0, 40, 64, 100, 100 % duty; values 80, 40, 12, 8, 8 fall as the duty rises, so the ramp slows toward full duty (at 650 rpm: about 372 counts = 1.5 % per pass at 0 % duty, about 56 counts = 0.2 % per pass above 64 %)
evidence: Statement pair wVar1 = lookup(rpm) ; wVar2 = lookup(duty) ; duty = duty + (short)((wVar1 * wVar2) / 10) in the state 3 branch after cruise_voltage_debounce_timer reaches 0 with cruise_voltage_fault_state != 1; both inputs are named and their breakpoints fit.

output: local wVar1 in cm848_filterProtectionOutput: the other factor of the per-pass duty increment in state 3 after the hold (see L081). Table-driven mode only: with operating_mode_flags bit 0x20 set (this dump) the PI loop overwrites the duty in the same pass
units_check: 5 breakpoints 3840, 5120, 6000, 8400, 8800 counts = 480, 640, 750, 1050, 1100 rpm; values 31, 41, 102, 1280, 1280 rise with engine speed: a slow ramp at idle (so the engine is not loaded abruptly) and a fast one above 1050 rpm
evidence: Same statement pair as L081; engine speed breakpoints span idle to just above 1000 rpm and the values rise monotonically with speed, which fits a load response ramp that is gentler at idle.

input: fuel_pressure_sensor_reference = boost_pressure_fuel_working + boost_fuel_pressure_offset_lookup (L220), clamped to 0x75e = 1886 before the call; boost_pressure_fuel_working is sensor_channel3_value, the barometric pressure sensor (barometric_pressure_sensor_config, AMB SPN 108), or its default value on a fault; 0.0159 inHg (1/18.56 kPa) per count
output: governor_adjustment_input = signed altitude in feet (flag 2 = signed output; values go negative). Its readers use it as the x axis of altitude tables: governor_adjustment_compare (3 threshold tables on a 0..15000 ft axis in 1000 ft steps), cm848_boostCompensatedRpmGovernor (axis 0, 100, 300, 1000, 3000, 6000, 14000, 29035 - the last is the height of Mount Everest in feet) and fuel_demandBlend_weight_calc (axis -300, 0, 2000..12000)
units_check: 16 breakpoints 1105..1899 counts x 0.0159 = 17.6..30.2 inHg against values 14000, 13000, ..., 1000, 0, -300 ft: every pair matches the standard atmosphere (1105 -> 17.58 inHg = 14000 ft; 1293 -> 20.6 inHg = 10000 ft; 1624 -> 25.8 inHg = 4000 ft; 1880 -> 29.9 inHg = 0 ft; 1899 -> 30.2 inHg = -300 ft); values fall by 1000 ft per row
evidence: The pressure-to-altitude pairs follow the standard atmosphere to within a count or two, which also confirms the 0.0159 inHg scale and that the input is an ambient pressure; the three consumers (L017, L199, L208-L210) all index tables in feet.
naming_concern: governor_adjustment_input is an altitude estimate in feet, not a governor input; fuel_pressure_sensor_reference is the barometric (ambient) pressure plus a small offset, not a fuel pressure; boost_pressure_fuel_working is the barometric sensor value (sensor_channel3_value), not boost; boost_fuel_pressure_offset_lookup is an offset added to that barometric value.

reason: input is the EMA (ema_filter_state_t_003fb9f6) of boost_pressure_state_t_0040a406.reserved_0c, which cm848_fuelDemandErrorCalculation sets to an EMA of max(0, fuel_quantity_ema_filtered - fuel_quantity_ema); both of those come from cm848_loadBasedFuelAdjustment / cm848_throttleBasedFuelCalculation (rpm x factor x map correction / load, in an unclear scale), so the 0..7680 breakpoints (step 512) cannot be checked against a unit. The output is clear (boost_fuel_pressure_offset_lookup, 0..121 counts = 0..6.5 kPa added to the barometric pressure to form fuel_pressure_sensor_reference, see L219) and its quadratic shape (3, 4, 5, 8, 12, 18, 24, 32, 41, 51, 63, 76, 89, 105, 121) hints at a flow-squared pressure drop, but that is unproven; a name from the output alone would be a guess.

x is boost_pressure_timing_ema_filtered, a second EMA (boost_pressure_timing_filter_state) of the same reserved_0c quantity as L220 (unclear scale), so the 0..6528 breakpoints (step 384) have no checkable unit; y is vehicle_speed_copy (1/256 mph, 0..21760 = 0..85 mph in 5 mph steps, fits). The output boost_fuel_timing_target is not a timing: it is subtracted from fuel_demand_timing_input = sensor_channel20_value (an NTC curve at 0x592e6 / 0x5930e: 17024 .. -2560 = 266 .. -40 F in 1/64 F) and the signed first-order filtered difference becomes boost_fuel_demand_blend_a (y axis of L199 runs -3200..8000 = -50..125 F), so the grid value 640 = 10 F; sensor channel 20 is unidentified and the grid is flat, so no defensible base. Naming concern: the boost_fuel_timing_* names in hpcr_fuelFinal_exponentialAverage describe a temperature-scale difference, not timing.

input: x engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (0.125 rpm per count); y fuel_demand_limit (fuel quantity limit, 0.0679 mm3 per count)
output: boost_fuel_rpm_blend_scale, read only by cm848_blendBoostAndThrottleFuelDemand as DAT_0040af78 = DAT_0040af76 * boost_fuel_rpm_blend_scale >> 10, i.e. a Q10 multiplier (1024 = 1.0, not Q12 here). The scaled term DAT_0040af76 is a lookup (table 0x4071e0 / 0x40720c) of boost_fuel_demand_blend_a clamped to 5760; the scaled value is divided by fuel_pressure_sensor_reference (barometric pressure) into a ratio clamped to 0x1000, which enters the blend weights fuel_demand_blend_weight_ema / _filtered; those weights multiply map_fuel_correction_factor (>> 8), a fuel correction taken from the boost pressure sensor value
units_check: x 19 breakpoints 6400..20800 counts = 800..2600 rpm in 100 rpm steps; y 16 breakpoints 0..2208 in steps of 147 = 10 mm3 (0..150 mm3); grid 19 x 16 = 304 values, all 1024 = 1.0 (a neutral scale in this calibration)
evidence: Both inputs are named and their breakpoints are exact multiples of 100 rpm and 10 mm3; the destination name is kept as the base because the code shows a scale multiplier whose consumer builds a blend weight for the boost-based fuel correction, but the physical identity of the scaled term is not established.
naming_concern: Evidenced words of boost_fuel_rpm_blend_scale: scale (Q10 multiplier), rpm (x axis), blend (it enters the blend weight computation), boost / fuel (the weighted factor comes from the boost pressure sensor value). Inherited and unproven: what the scaled term DAT_0040af76 physically is (looked up from a 1/64 F temperature-scale difference, then divided by the barometric reference); the table also depends on fuel_demand_limit, which the name omits. Neighbours are doubtful: boost_fuel_demand_blend_a is a temperature-scale difference (sensor channel 20 minus the L221 target) and governor_adjustment_input is an altitude.
